title: They almost killed Him… in church.
paragraphs: They almost killed Him… in church.

Not in the streets.
Not in a battlefield.
In a place where Scripture was read.
And that should disturb you.
Because the same spirit still lives today.

You can sit in the presence of truth…
and still resist it.

You can hear Jesus…
and still want Him gone.

Not out loud.
But in your heart.
Look again at that moment.
“All those in the synagogue, when they heard these things, were filled with wrath… and led Him to the brow of the hill… that they might throw Him down over the cliff.”
Pause.
These weren’t outsiders.

These were listeners.
Regulars.
People who knew the sound of Scripture.

They didn’t explode when Jesus healed.
They didn’t react when He spoke kindly.
They snapped when He exposed them.
That’s the tension.
We love a Jesus who comforts.
We struggle with a Jesus who confronts.

We celebrate grace…
until grace demands repentance.

We post verses…
until those verses point at us.
And suddenly…

The same lips that say “Amen”
start whispering, “Too much.”
Let me ask you something that might shake you:
What part of Jesus are you secretly resisting?
Is it His call to forgive someone who hurt you?
“For if you forgive others… your heavenly Father will also forgive you.”
Is it His command to walk away from a hidden sin?
“For this is the will of God, your sanctification…”
Is it His authority over your plans, your desires, your control?
“If anyone would come after Me, let him deny himself and take up his cross daily…”
Because here’s the truth we don’t like to say out loud:
Sometimes we don’t reject Jesus completely.
We just try to push Him to the edge.
That’s what Nazareth did.

They didn’t deny He spoke well.
They didn’t deny His power.
They just refused His authority.

They wanted inspiration…
not surrender.

They wanted miracles…
not transformation.

They wanted a Savior…
but not a Lord.
And before you point at them—
Look inward.
Because pride doesn’t always shout.

Sometimes it sits quietly in church…
arms crossed…
heart closed.

Sometimes it sings worship songs
while resisting conviction.

Sometimes it looks holy on the outside
but is negotiating obedience on the inside.
That is the most dangerous place to be.
Close to Jesus.
But unmoved by Him.
Here’s the weight of it:
Their anger wasn’t random.
Jesus confronted their assumption that they deserved special favor.
He reminded them that God’s grace reached outsiders.
That stung their pride.
Some scholars interpret this moment as a direct challenge to religious entitlement—Jesus exposing the human tendency to think we are “worthy” while others are not.
And that exposure triggered rage.
Because pride doesn’t like being dethroned.
But don’t miss this.
Don’t miss this.
Jesus walked away from that cliff.
“But passing through the midst of them, He went away.”
Why?
Because it wasn’t time.
The cross was still ahead.
And when that time came…
He didn’t walk away.
He walked toward it.
That’s the Gospel.

The same Jesus they tried to throw away
chose to be lifted up on a cross.
Not forced.
Willing.
“No one takes it from Me, but I lay it down of My own accord.”
He took the rejection.
He absorbed the wrath.
He carried the sin—not just of violent crowds—
But of quiet resistance.
Of hidden pride.
Of selective obedience.
Of hearts that say, “I’ll follow You… but only this far.”
And this is where everything turns.
Because the story doesn’t end at the cliff.
It ends at an empty tomb.
“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Not when we were fully surrendered.
Not when we had it all together.
While we were still resisting Him.
That means this:
Even if you’ve been pushing Jesus to the edges of your life…
He is still reaching for you.
Even if you’ve been avoiding the parts of truth that confront you…
Grace is still calling your name.
Even if pride has been sitting on the throne of your heart…
There is still a King who invites you to step down—and be free.
This is your moment.
Not to admire Jesus.
Not to analyze Him.
But to surrender.
Fully.
No conditions.
No hidden corners.
No “except this part.”
Because partial surrender is still resistance.
Let Him be Lord.
Not just Savior.
Let Him confront you.
Not to shame you—
But to free you.
Because every command of Christ is not a cage.
It’s a key.
So here’s the question that won’t leave you:
Are you drawing closer to Jesus…
Or quietly pushing Him away?
Stop.
Pray.
Be honest.
“Jesus, I surrender the part of me that resists You.”
